Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- TTFT: our UX team is pushing for p50 <=150ms and p95 <=300ms for the primary chat flow. For background batch/async jobs (e.g., nightly summarization) the TTFT constraints are looser.
- Throughput: target sustained 2000 req/s for normal traffic; yes we need bursts to ~8k for campaign spikes.
- Concurrency: expecting ~200 concurrent active streaming sessions (each long-lived SSE connection).
- Streaming: must support both SSE and WebSocket (we use SSE for web client, WS for mobile fallback). Chunk cadence: target <=300ms between user-visible chunks; prefer ~200-250ms if achievable.
- Payloads: typical request ~30-80 input tokens, responses average 40-120 tokens; we can provide a sample dataset.

Happy to run the sample payloads through whatever test harness you propose. Please include any rate-limiting/connection guidance.

Thanks Marissa / Mike — copying internal follow-up items here. Proposed initial approach for lab validation:

1) Model & config
- Start with a mid-sized autoregressive model (redwood-ozone-7b-quant) for throughput/TTFT balance. If TTFT/p95 targets require, evaluate a lower-latency variant (ozone-rt-3b) during next iteration.
- Quantization profile: 4-bit where acceptable, with fallback to 8-bit for quality-critical paths.

2) Serving runtime tunables
- Continuous batching with strict max-batch-latency 30ms to avoid batch-induced TTFT spikes.
- KV prefix caching for common system prompts to shave ~20-40ms off TTFT.
- Dedicated pool for streaming endpoints to avoid cold resource contention.

3) Networking/streaming
- Support SSE and WebSocket endpoints. For SSE: send initial headers immediately and flush first chunk within 120-150ms when possible.
- Chunk cadence target: 200-300ms inter-chunk for progressive rendering; ensure heartbeat/stall packets every 5s to keep connections alive under proxies.

4) Load/profile parameters for lab run
- Sustained phase: 2k req/s for 10 minutes.
- Burst phase: ramp to 8k req/s over 30s, hold 60s, then ramp down.
- Concurrency: emulate 200 long-lived clients with pipelined shorter requests to simulate background ops.
- Payloads: use Mike's sample distribution (30-80 input tokens, 40-120 output tokens).

Action items for internal: Sean to write the test harness and schedule infra; Rachel to prepare a tracing/metrics dashboard for p50/p95 TTFT and chunk cadence; I will map config knobs and expected unit costs.

Dev
